Title: Sunway Construction's unit clinches RM920mil variation works contract in Johor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd's wholly owned unit Sunway Construction Sdn Bhd has received a letter of award for variation (LOAV) works from a US-headquartered multinational technology corporation worth approximately RM920.8 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the construction group said the variation works involve additional mechanical, electrical, and plumbing fit-out works for the ongoing development of a data centre in Johor.
"The LOAV also serves as the instruction to commence the variation works, which are targeted to be completed by the first quarter in 2028 (Q1 2028)," it said.
The group said the variation works contract will not affect the group's share capital or substantial shareholders' shareholdings, as no new shares will be allotted or issued under the variation works.
"The variation works are not expected to have any immediate material effect on the earnings per share, net assets per share and gearing of the group for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
"However, barring any unforeseen circumstances, the variation works are expected to contribute positively to the earnings of the group for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, onwards," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FDS still grounded amid reports of helicopter's emergency landing in Bintulu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) in Sarawak has yet to resume operations and is still undergoing further scrutiny and assessment before any decision is made on its reactivation.
The Health Ministry said any resumption of the service would have to take into account operational safety, the welfare of personnel and staff readiness.
"The Health Ministry emphasises that the FDS in Sarawak has yet to resume operations and is still undergoing further scrutiny and assessment before any decision is made on its reactivation.
"Any resumption of the service must take into account operational safety, the welfare of personnel and staff readiness," it said when contacted.
This comes after a
helicopter was seen
making an emergency landing in Bintulu today following a minor technical problem while travelling from Sibu to Miri, according to a report by Borneo Post.
Bintulu police chief Superintendent Nixon Joshua Ali said the helicopter was heading to Miri to take part in an exhibition programme when the incident occurred at about 3.20pm.
"The helicopter made an emergency landing due to a minor technical problem. There were no Health Ministry passengers, only the pilot and two crew members," he told the regional paper.
The incident went viral after a 51-second video showing the helicopter landing in an open area near the housing estate circulated on social media.
The video, uploaded to the Bintulu News Page 2 Facebook page, showed the helicopter on an open field next to the housing estate.
The FDS suspension followed a
helicopter crash in Long Lellang
, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8, which killed all five people on board.
The BO-105 helicopter, bearing registration number 9M-LLF, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) port around 3.40pm while carrying a pilot and four Health Ministry personnel.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
Following the tragedy, the Health Ministry
suspended all FDS operations
in Sarawak to allow investigations and a reassessment of the service's safety aspects and operational mechanisms.
It is understood that the helicopter's operator would be issuing a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,500 oil palm smallholders to benefit from replanting financing incentive scheme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,500 independent smallholders, covering 5,900ha, are expected to benefit from the Smallholder Oil Palm Replanting Financing Incentive Scheme (TSPKS) 2.0 under the 2027 Budget.
Plantations and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said the programme aims to support independent smallholders in replanting activities and strengthen the sustainability of the oil palm sector.
"In addition, 740 independent oil palm smallholders, with a combined cultivation area of 11,110 hectares, are expected to benefit from the Oil Palm Replanting Financing Programme (PTSS)," she said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in Dewan Rakyat today.
Under the 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced an allocation of RM200 million for TSPKS 2.0.
The government will also continue the PTSS, which provides financial assistance to eligible smallholders facing capital constraints.
Meanwhile, on the income of rubber smallholders, Noraini said that their actual earnings were influenced by production levels, including tapping frequency and the size of their plantations.
"The ministry will continue to maintain the rubber production incentive (IPG) as an income-guarantee mechanism based on the activation pricing level (PHP).
"Smallholders will benefit from the IPG, particularly when prices fall below the PHP threshold," she said, adding that the IPG price threshold had been increased seven times since 2015.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: No instructions from Bersatu to supporters to back PH
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu has not issued any instructions to its grassroots members to support Pakatan Harapan candidates in seats where there is no contest between the two coalitions in the Melaka election.
Its vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu said although the party had not issued any instructions to its members and supporters, it appreciated PH's willingness to support its candidates.
"Although (Melaka Pakatan Harapan chairman) Adly Zahari had stated openly that his side had no objection to supporting us in seats it is not contesting, we have not issued any instructions on our part.
"At the same time, however, we are grateful that PH leaders have expressed such a willingness," he said when met while campaigning in the Ayer Keroh constituency here.
Adly had previously said the coalition had
no objection
to its supporters backing Bersatu candidates in state seats it was not contesting.
He was reported to have said that although there was no formal cooperation between PH and Bersatu, the approach was intended to minimise clashes with the party led by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, while allowing such support to take place.
In a separate development, Ahmad Faizal said Bersatu was hopeful of retaining the two seats it won in the 2021 state election, namely Sungai Udang and Bemban.
He said the target was realistic, based on the preparations made by the party's machinery at all levels.
"Based on what we can see in terms of the machinery's preparations and other factors, I hope securing two or three seats is not impossible.
"If we thought we would get the same result (as in Negri Sembilan), I do not think we would have fielded candidates.
"However, if the results do not go our way, we will continue to strive. Our struggle does not end with the Melaka election," he said.
In the 2021 Melaka election, Bersatu won two seats, namely Sungai Udang and Bemban.
This time, the party is contesting seven seats, compared with its initial plan to field candidates in eight, after making way for Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia in Gadek.
On its last-minute decision to withdraw from the contest in Gadek, Ahmad Faizal said it was made because coordination issues could not be resolved in time.
"The decision was made after taking into account the preparations of the party machinery and the readiness of our ally to contest in the constituency.
"We have also asked our members and supporters in Gadek to support the Putra candidate as part of the cooperation between the two parties under the Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR) coalition," he said.
Asked whether the Melaka election could serve as a test for more formal cooperation between PH and Bersatu ahead of future elections, Ahmad Faizal said his party was open to discussions with any party that shared similar ideals and objectives.
Meanwhile, he said Bersatu still regarded itself as part of Perikatan Nasional, despite statements by several coalition leaders questioning the party's position.
This follows the issue surrounding the cancellation of PN's registration by the Registrar of Societies (ROS).
He said that, based on his understanding of the PN constitution, Bersatu remained part of the coalition, and any differences of opinion should be resolved through discussions and negotiations between the party leaderships.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RON97 price drops by 20 sen, RON95 and diesel down by 15 sen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail price of RON97 will drop by 20 sen to RM4.70 per litre, while unsubsidised RON95 and diesel will go down 15 sen to RM4.27 and RM5.12 per litre for the period of Nov 5 to 11.
The Finance Ministry, in a statement today, announced that this pricing is determined based on the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) formula.
"The regional petroleum market shows signs of moderation following an increase in the supply of refined fuels, including petrol and diesel stocks in Singapore, which serves as one of the market references for petroleum pricing in Malaysia.
"This development, together with the drop in Brent crude oil prices at the end of the APM calculation period, indicates the possibility of lower price pressures," the ministry said in a statement.
However, it said geopolitical uncertainties in the Middle East continue to pose risks to world petroleum price stability.
Meanwhile, the price of subsidised RON95 through Budi95 remains at RM1.99 per litre, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.28 per litre, or 53 per cent of the unsubsidised price for the period.
For Budi Diesel, the price for eligible recipients remains at RM2.10 per litre, involving a government subsidy of RM3.02 per litre, or 59 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
Additionally, the price of petrol under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) remains at RM2.05 per litre, while diesel under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) remains at RM2.15 per litre.
According to the ministry, eligible Malaysians can continue to purchase subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad, subject to monthly eligibility limits.
"The government will continue to take a prudent approach to protect the rakyat from price fluctuations, while ensuring that the country's fuel supply remains adequate and secure," the statement added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jati Tinggi enters energy storage with TNB contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jati Tinggi Group Bhd is entering the battery energy storage system (BESS) sector after securing a RM2.9 million contract from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) for a community energy storage system project.
Its wholly-owned subsidiary Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd will undertake the project through an unincorporated joint venture with Reactive Energy Sdn Bhd.
The contract involves supplying, installing, testing and commissioning a 150kW/430kWh community energy storage system under TNB's Pulau Tenaga Hijau initiative, which focuses on the distribution network.
The system comprises battery storage, power conversion, energy management and control systems.
It is designed to store excess solar energy for subsequent use within the distribution network while supporting renewable energy integration and off-grid or microgrid applications.
Under the joint venture arrangement, Jati Tinggi Holding will hold a 55 per cent stake, with Reactive Energy owning the remaining 45 per cent.
Both parties will jointly execute and complete the project.
The project is expected to be completed within 18 months from its commencement date.
Managing director Datuk Wira Lim Yeong Seong said the contract will extend Jati Tinggi's capabilities beyond conventional power infrastructure into energy storage technologies.
He said the project will also help the company build technical expertise and establish a track record in BESS solutions.
Lim said growing adoption of renewable energy was creating opportunities for energy storage systems, particularly in integrating renewable power sources and improving grid reliability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KEB IPO fully subscribed ahead of Nov 16 listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KEB Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) has been fully subscribed ahead of its listing on the ACE Market on Nov 16.
KEB's IPO comprises 226.78 million shares, consisting of a public issue of 138.54 million new shares and an offer for sale of 88.24 million existing shares.
The company said it received 2,126 applications for 44.47 million shares from the Malaysian public, and these were fully subscribed.
A total of 1,071 applications for 27.31 million shares for the Bumiputera portion, while it received 1,055 applications for 17.16 million shares for the other Malaysian public portion.
Managing director Datuk Lim Kim Chong said the response reflects investor confidence in KEB's business fundamentals, track record and future prospects.
"This support is meaningful to us as we prepare for our ACE Market debut and embark on the next phase of our growth journey.
"With our ongoing developments, future pipeline and landbank, we believe KEB is well positioned to continue building on the foundation we have established over the past two decades," he said in a statement.
KEB has completed 14 property development projects to date.
Its current pipeline comprises four ongoing developments with an estimated total gross development value (GDV) of about RM1.36 billion, alongside two future projects with an estimated total GDV of RM382.73 million.
Proceeds raised will be utilised for landbank acquisition for development, working capital for project development, repayment of bank borrowings, and defraying listing expenses.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: National cybersecurity threat level raised to moderate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has raised the National Cyber Threat Level (NCTL) from low to moderate as a precautionary measure in response to current security developments.
The National Security Council (NSC) said the move was aimed at ensuring the country's essential services remained protected against potential disruptions.
It said the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) held a meeting with sector leads and National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) entities this morning to strengthen preparedness and coordination across sectors.
"The meeting outlined nine cybersecurity preparedness measures for all NCII entities, including 24-hour monitoring, system patching, multi-factor authentication and updates to their Service Continuity Plans.
"NCII sector leads are also required to submit weekly threat status reports to NACSA.
"These cybersecurity preparedness measures were also presented at a special meeting of ministry secretaries-general and heads of service yesterday," it said in a statement.
Meanwhile, Nacsa, through the National Cyber Coordination and Command Centre (NC4), is continuously carrying out three key tasks: issuing cybersecurity alerts and advisories, strengthening threat detection and assessment capabilities, and monitoring the cybersecurity of NCII entities and government agencies.
The NSC said NC4 issued eight alerts and advisories in October on vulnerabilities affecting NCII entities and government agencies.
The measures would allow preventive and mitigation action to be taken earlier to reduce the risk of disruptions to the country's essential services.
"The government remains committed to safeguarding the country's security, stability and sovereignty through comprehensive, integrated and continuous preparedness measures to protect the people and national interests," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ni Hsin unit partners China's Horwin for electric motorcycle venture
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ni Hsin Group Bhd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Ni Hsin EV Tech Sdn Bhd (NHEVT), has signed an agreement with China's Horwin International Inc to manufacture and exclusively distribute electric motorcycles in Malaysia and Turkey.
In a statement today, the diversified manufacturer said Horwin would supply chassis for two electric motorcycle models, the SK3 and SK3 Plus, on a completely knocked-down basis under the agreement.
"NHEVT will assemble the motorcycles at its manufacturing and assembly facilities in Seri Kembangan, Selangor, incorporating 50 per cent locally sourced components.
"The finished electric motorcycles will be classified as 'Malaysian-made' and will qualify for export to Turkey under the Malaysia-Turkey Free Trade Agreement," it said.
NHEVT managing director Khoo Chee Kong said the collaboration marked a significant milestone in the company's efforts to establish itself as a key player in the electric motorcycle industry.
He said the partnership would expand NHEVT's product portfolio while contributing to the global shift towards greener transportation.
The agreement was signed at the EIMCA Global EV trade show in Milan, Italy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Helicopter seen making emergency landing in Bintulu
Article:
KUCHING: A helicopter was suspected to have made a landing in an open area near the Sri Pertiwi housing estate in Kidurong, Bintulu, today.
The incident went viral after a 51-second video showing the helicopter landing in an open area near the housing estate circulated on social media.
The video, uploaded to the Bintulu News Page 2 Facebook page, showed the helicopter on an open field next to the housing estate.
Sarawak acting police commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak, when contacted, said police had so far received no information about the incident.
"However, investigations are ongoing," he said.
The incident has renewed public attention on Flying Doctor Services operations in Sarawak, particularly following a helicopter crash involving the service that claimed five lives in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8.
It is understood that the operator would be issuing a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boy, 6, drowns after falling into Kulai retention pond while fishing
Article:
KULAI: A 6-year-old boy drowned after falling into a retention pond while fishing at Kampung Melayu Kulai here today.
The boy was pronounced dead at the scene.
Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Awang Adzwan Awang Sahari said an emergency call was made at 10.17am.
He said six firemen were deployed to the scene and arrived seven minutes later.
They used ropes and a stretcher to retrieve the body of the boy from the pond and later handed over the remains to police.
The
New Straits Times
has contacted district police for further details but has yet to receive a response.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No by-election for Mata Ayer seat - Speaker
Article:
KANGAR: No by-election will be held for the Mata Ayer state seat following the death of its incumbent, Wan Badariah Wan Saad, on Saturday, as more than three years have elapsed since the current Perlis state legislative assembly first convened.
Perlis state assembly speaker Rus'sele Eizan said the first meeting of the first session of the 15th assembly was held on Dec 19, 2022, meaning the three-year period was completed on Dec 18, 2025.
He said the vacancy would not affect the majority held by the parties forming the state government.
"Currently, the Perlis state assembly has 11 members, comprising five from Pas, five from Bersatu and one from Pakatan Harapan (PH), representing PKR. The state government remains under Perikatan Nasional (PN), comprising Pas and Bersatu.
"None of the assemblymen has withdrawn support for Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah. Therefore, the state administration continues to function as usual under his leadership," he told Bernama today.
Rus'sele said he had submitted official notification of the vacancy to the Perlis Election Commission (EC) today.
Wan Badariah
, 50, died at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) at 4.26pm last Saturday.
In the 15th general election (GE15), she secured 4,419 votes as the PN candidate for Pas, defeating Barisan Nasional's (BN) Siti Berenee Yahaya, who received 2,398 votes, and Pakatan Harapan's (PH) Amran Kamarudin, who garnered 794 votes, with a majority of 2,021.
She had previously served as chairman of the Perlis Tourism, Culture, Arts and Heritage Committee under former menteri besar Mohd Shukri Ramli.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Binastra lands RM304mil Klang warehouse job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Binastra Corp Bhd's unit Binastra Builders Sdn Bhd has secured a RM303.8 million contract from PTT Synexis Sdn Bhd to build an automated storage and retrieval system warehouse facility in Klang.
The company said the contract is an opportunity to broaden its construction portfolio into specialised industrial infrastructure and strengthen its capabilities in delivering complex, technology-enabled warehouse facilities.
The scope of work includes piling and construction of a single-storey warehouse with a mezzanine floor, a three-storey office building, two mechanical and electrical buildings, a five-storey car park, a container yard depot and other ancillary facilities.
Construction is scheduled to commence on Nov 11, with completion expected in less than 11 months.
Binastra Corp managing director Datuk Jackson Tan Kak Seng said the project represents a strategic step towards broadening the company's capabilities beyond its established core business and expanding into specialised industrial infrastructure.
"We see this as an exciting new opportunity for the group and intend to actively explore further opportunities in industrial and technology-driven construction as we continue to diversify our project portfolio.
"We recognise that the warehousing and logistics sector is evolving, driven by the continued growth of the fast-moving consumer goods, manufacturing and retail industries, alongside increasing demand for greater supply chain efficiency, storage optimisation and operational productivity.
"These developments are creating demand for modern, purpose-built facilities with more sophisticated infrastructure and technological requirements," he said.
With this latest contract win, Binastra's year-to-date contract wins have reached RM1.6 billion.
This brings its total outstanding order book to RM6.2 billion, providing earnings visibility for up to three years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit closes higher against greenback ahead of OPR decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit edged up against the US dollar and other Asean currencies at Wednesday's closing ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia's overnight policy rate (OPR) decision tomorrow.
The Monetary Policy Committee will hold its sixth and final policy meeting of 2026 on Nov 5.
At 6pm, the local note rose to 4.0610/0660 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0735/0775.
According to reports, research firms expect Bank Negara to maintain the OPR at 2.75 per cent tomorrow and throughout 2027, supported by resilient economic growth and a manageable inflation outlook.
It said headline inflation is expected to remain comfortably within central bank's projected range of 1.5 to 2.5 per cent in the near term.
On the external front, SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the ringgit was on firmer footing following the Democratic Party's gains in the US Mid-Term Elections.
He said a Democratic sweep of US Congress could provide modest support for Asian currencies, including the ringgit, as increased political gridlock in Washington could reduce the likelihood of further US fiscal expansion, potentially weighing on US Treasury yields and the US dollar.
"However, for the ringgit to make more meaningful gains, we would probably need to see markets start pricing out some of the odds of a December US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.
"The complication is that President Donald Trump's tariffs remain largely under presidential control, so the election result does not necessarily remove the inflation pressures that could prevent the Fed from shifting toward a more dovish stance. That may limit how far the US dollar can fall, at least initially," he told Bernama.
Similarly, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment appeared to have improved following the US Mid-Term Elections result as the Trump administration could face greater legislative hurdles in passing new laws, although the US President retains veto powers.
"Consequently, the US Dollar Index fell 0.46 per cent to 101.399 points. It is still too early to tell whether the elections result would see significant shift in US policies especially in relation to trade and the ongoing war in Iran.
"For now, markets are quite constructive which to some degree, may have resulted in improved risk appetite. Therefore, the ringgit was gaining by 0.20 per cent to RM4.06 today," he said.
Against major currencies, the ringgit traded mostly lower.
The ringgit was higher against the Japanese yen to 2.5636/5669 from 2.5762/5789 at Tuesday's close but inched down versus the euro to 4.5723/5779 from 4.5587/5631, and edged down vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4783/4850 from 5.4658/4712 previously.
However, the ringgit strengthened against its Asean peers.
It gained against the Singapore dollar to 3.1771/1813 from the previous close of 3.1807/1841, rose versus the Thai baht to 12.0673/0868 from 12.0696/0858 yesterday, inched up against the rupiah to 223.5/223.8 from 224.3/224.6, and climbed vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.39/6.40 from 6.42/6.43 previously.

Title: Asean pushes for stronger media ties amid AI risks
Article:
FUZHOU: Asean and its Plus Three partners - China, Japan and South Korea,  must strengthen media cooperation and promote responsible artificial intelligence (AI) governance to safeguard information integrity and public trust amid rapid digital transformation.
Asean secretary-general Dr Kao Kim Hourn said the growing influence of AI in shaping how information is produced, distributed and consumed has made it increasingly important for media organisations to uphold accuracy, transparency and accountability.
He said while AI offers significant opportunities for the media industry, its rapid advancement also raises serious concerns over misinformation, manipulation, privacy and public safety.
"Media professionals have an important role to play. They can reflect diverse perspectives, safeguard privacy, and help the public distinguish credible information from misinformation and manipulation," he said at the 12th Asean Plus Three (APT) Media Cooperation Forum here. Kao delivered his speech in a pre-recorded video.
The APT Media Cooperation Forum was held in conjunction  with the 2026 Media Cooperation Forum on the Belt and Road.
Kao said Asean has taken concrete steps to strengthen responsible AI governance through several regional initiatives, including the Asean Guide on AI Governance and Ethics, the Asean Responsible AI Roadmap and the Asean AI Safety Network.
He said these initiatives reflect Asean's commitment to harnessing the benefits of emerging technologies while ensuring their development and application remain safe, responsible and people-centred.
In the media and information sector, he said Asean has embarked on a new 10-year work plan aimed at improving access to information, strengthening information integrity and addressing challenges arising from digital transformation and AI.
The regional grouping also intends to develop a new work plan with its Plus Three partners to expand cooperation in the media and information sector, including through stronger partnerships and cross-sectoral collaboration.
Beyond technological challenges, Kao emphasised the importance of strengthening professional networks among journalists across Asean, China, Japan and South Korea to promote accurate, responsible and context-driven reporting on regional developments.
He said capacity-building programmes, personnel exchanges and joint reporting initiatives could enhance professional standards while fostering greater understanding among media practitioners from different countries.
Kao also underscored the media's broader responsibility in translating regional cooperation into meaningful narratives that resonate with ordinary citizens.
"For many of our citizens, regional cooperation is not experienced through official documents or communiqués. It is experienced through the stories they read, watch and share.
"How those stories are told can shape whether Asean Plus Three is seen as a distant process, or as a partnership that makes a real difference in daily life," he said.
As regional economies and societies become increasingly interconnected, Kao said the media plays a crucial role in helping the public understand both the opportunities and challenges of deeper cooperation.
Kao said the forum's emphasis on strengthening the Asean Plus Three mechanism, deepening economic and trade cooperation, and promoting mutual learning among civilisations was particularly timely.
He added that Asean Plus Three remains one of the region's most substantive and enduring cooperation frameworks, with achievements spanning financial stability, public health, food security, connectivity and people-to-people exchanges.
The APT Media Cooperation Forum, organised by China's People's Daily, brought together leaders of mainstream media organisations, scholars, experts and business leaders from Asean Plus Three countries to exchange perspectives on regional media cooperation and emerging challenges in the information landscape.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Clean-up assistance, aid given to Kampung Melayu Subang flood victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Clean-up operations are underway for flood victims in Kampung Melayu Subang following the latest flash floods, the fourth such incident in the area within 30 days.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan, who is also Sungai Buloh member of parliament, aid was also in the works for affected residents.
He said a temporary relief centre (PPS) had been opened while cleaning operations at affected homes were being carried out.
"The prime minister himself went down yesterday to visit the victims to ensure that all assistance was provided immediately," he said.
Ramanan said the government was also looking at expediting the construction of a retention pond to address the recurring flash floods as the frequency of the incidents was a cause for concern.
He said the authorities would continue coordinating assistance for affected residents while efforts were being made to find a longer-term solution to the flooding problem.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Weststar delivers first AW139 helicopter to Fire and Rescue Dept
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Weststar Aviation Sdn Bhd has delivered the first Leonardo AW139 helicopter to the Fire and Rescue Department under a government leasing concession covering 28 helicopters for various agencies.
The helicopter was officially handed over on Nov 4 at a ceremony officiated by Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming in Subang.
The concession agreement, signed between the government and Weststar Aviation in December 2024, took effect on June 16, 2025.
It requires Weststar to supply 28 helicopters to government agencies over three years.
Nga said the leasing arrangement is expected to save the government about RM3 billion compared with conventional aircraft procurement.
Under the 15-year concession, the concessionaire will also be responsible for aircraft maintenance, reducing the government's direct maintenance obligations.
The AW139 will support the department's search and rescue operations, firefighting, medical evacuations, patient transportation and logistical assistance during emergencies and disasters.
Weststar and the department completed the aircraft's pre-delivery inspection and final acceptance test. It is now ready for operational deployment.
Weststar Aviation chief executive officer General Tan Sri Muhammad Ismail Jamaluddin said the delivery followed close coordination between the government, the department, Leonardo Helicopters and the company's teams.
The second AW139 helicopter allocated to the department is scheduled to arrive in Malaysia by the end of November, with operational deployment targeted for mid-December, ahead of the peak monsoon season.
The leasing programme will cover several government agencies involved in defence, security, law enforcement, firefighting and emergency response.
Under the arrangement, Weststar will provide the helicopters, maintenance and related support throughout the concession period.
This allows government agencies to access aircraft without substantial upfront capital expenditure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NRD steps up efforts to make MyKad address updates easier
Article:
MELAKA: The National Registration Department (NRD) has introduced various initiatives to make identity documentation services easier, faster and more efficient for the public.
In a Facebook post, the NRD said one of the initiatives was its participation in the Digital Village Programme to help residents update their residential addresses on their MyKad, ensuring that their identification details were accurate and up to date.
"Among the achievements recorded were the registration of 618 traditional villages in Melaka, the distribution of address stickers to 26,711 premises across 187 villages, as at July 2025, and the receipt of 7,295 applications for MyKad address changes from last year until September this year," the post read.
The NRD said its 'Menyemai Kasih Rakyat' (Mekar) initiative had also expanded its service coverage to reach more people in need.
"This reflects the NRD's continued commitment to ensuring that national registration services remain accessible, convenient and beneficial to all segments of society," it said.
Meanwhile, the Prisons Department said in a Facebook post that reintegration was not merely about preparing inmates for release, but also an important step towards building confidence, responsibility and positive relationships between inmates and the community.
It said the Prison Inmate Reintegration Programme (PRPP) at the Jasin Correctional Centre continued to strengthen inmates' preparations to readjust to life in the community.
"This commitment is also reflected in various corporate social responsibility (CSR) programmes, including gotong-royong activities at the Seri Murni Community-Based Rehabilitation Centre (PPDK), a Quran Appreciation Programme, mushroom cultivation and gotong-royong activities at SMK Tebong.
"These initiatives demonstrate that prisons play a role not only in security and rehabilitation, but also in contributing to community well-being," the post said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FDI vital to Malaysia's economic growth, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign direct investment (FDI) is crucial to Malaysia's economic growth, helping expand the economy, develop modern infrastructure and strengthen the country's position in the global artificial intelligence (AI) landscape.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this while commending Google for its US$15 billion investment commitment in Malaysia.
He said foreign investments must align with the Ekonomi Madani framework.
"FDI is vital, and its full power is realised when it elevates our fundamental pillars: building a globally competitive economy, developing our people, and ethically managing our natural resources," he said at the Mantap Malaysia Bersama AI event at Universiti Malaya's Chancellery building.
Earlier,
Google announced plans
to invest US$15 billion in Malaysia between 2027 and 2028 to develop digital infrastructure, including data centre campuses in industrial zones, expand clean energy capacity and strengthen local water security.
Anwar said the project would boost the country's gross domestic product and create local employment during its construction phase, while its operations would offer high-value jobs with wages above the national median.
He also highlighted Google's commitment to upskill 800,000 Malaysians and support technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions through practical, high-tech training.
Anwar also commended Google's water stewardship project, which includes the construction of an off-river storage reservoir and a water treatment plant capable of supplying 65 million litres of potable water daily.
"This is to reduce monsoon flood risks, and secure water reserves during dry seasons.
​
"Upon completion, ownership of these facilities will be handed over directly to the state government as a permanent public asset," he said.

Title: Customs seize RM2.24mil worth of drugs in Selangor, Kelantan operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor Customs Department has foiled an attempt to smuggle 44.5kg of ketamine worth more than RM2.22 million into the country through courier parcels falsely declared as medical supplies and marine equipment.
The seizure was made during an inspection of three imported courier parcels at a courier company's mail processing centre in Sepang on Aug 13 under Op Mekong Dragon VII.
Selangor Customs director Noraidah Ishak said the three parcels, which carried different air waybills, were believed to have been imported from a European country and addressed to recipients in Sepang.
"An inspection of the first parcel uncovered 15 plastic packages containing suspected ketamine weighing 15.265kg, while another 15 packages weighing 15.236kg were found in the second parcel.
"The third parcel contained 14 packages of suspected ketamine weighing 14kg, bringing the total seizure to 44.501kg with an estimated value of RM2,225,050," she said in a statement today.
Noraidah said investigations revealed that the syndicate had attempted to evade Customs detection by making false declarations on the air waybills.
She said the first two parcels were declared as containing elastic compression bandages, non-sterile fabrics, standard acoustic stethoscopes and non-electronic dual respirators.
The third parcel was declared as containing a plastic marine air filter.
All the seized items were taken to the North Port Customs Office.
In a separate case, Noraidah said Customs officers seized 286g of suspected cannabis buds worth RM22,880 following a motorcycle chase in Jeli, Kelantan, on Oct 13.
She said the seizure was made under Op Shieldgate when enforcement officers spotted a suspicious motorcycle without a registration number.
"Upon realising that he was being followed, the motorcyclist attempted to escape, triggering a chase involving Customs enforcement officers.
"The suspect managed to escape through a narrow road but threw a green plastic package by the roadside while fleeing," she said.
An inspection of the discarded package uncovered suspected cannabis buds weighing 0.286kg.
Noraidah said the suspect was believed to have used a motorcycle without a registration number to avoid detection and facilitate his escape if his activities were discovered.
The seized drugs were taken to the North Port Customs Office for further investigation.
She said the two operations resulted in the seizure of 44.787kg of suspected drugs with a combined estimated value of RM2,247,930.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment and at least 12 strokes of the cane if the death penalty is not imposed.
She said information on suspected smuggling activities could be channelled through the Customs toll-free hotline at 1-800-88-8855 or the nearest Customs office.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED]: STR Phase 4 payments to be disbursed from today — Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced that the fourth phase of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) payments will be disbursed from today.
He said the RM1.1 billion in assistance, provided in conjunction with Deepavali, would benefit more than five million people, including 630,000 recipients from the Indian community.
Anwar said the Indian community should not view assistance channelled through the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (Mitra) as its only source of support.
"I want to emphasise this so everyone understands: Malays, Chinese, Indians, Orang Asli, Sikhs — everyone is included.
"For the Indian community specifically, there are 630,000 STR recipients," he said at the Mega Bazaar Deepavali 2026 in Brickfields.
Anwar also said Mitra's annual allocation increased by 50 per cent to RM150 million, from RM100 million, with priority given to skills training and job opportunities for Indian youths in industrial automation, technology and aircraft maintenance.
He said financing for Indian entrepreneurs was also expanded to RM150 million.
This comprised RM100 million under Tekun Nasional's Indian Community Entrepreneur Development Scheme (SPUMI) and RM50 million in Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) microfinancing for Indian women entrepreneurs.
The government also allocated an additional RM50 million for the maintenance and repair of SJKTs.
This includes a complete replacement school for SJKT Ladang Pamol in Kluang, Johor, and six new SJKT projects, including those in Sungai Bakap, Penang, and Klebang, Perak, some of which are nearing completion.
Anwar said an additional RM80 million was also approved this year for temples and houses of worship.
To date, STR and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) disbursements have reached RM12 billion, while STR payments under Phases 1 to 3 amounted to RM3.6 billion.
During the
2027 Budget announcement
on Oct 9, Anwar said the allocation for STR and Sara would increase to RM16 billion next year, from RM15 billion this year.
Up to nine million STR recipients would also be eligible for monthly Sara assistance of up to RM150, or RM1,800 annually.

Title: 1,781 policemen on duty for Deepavali in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor police will deploy 1,781 personnel for a three-day security operation from Friday to ensure public safety during the Deepavali celebrations.
State police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the deployment involved 201 officers and 1,580 personnel who would monitor strategic locations.
He said Op Cahaya would focus on residential areas, entertainment outlets, shopping malls, Hindu temples, major highways and international entry points, including the Johor Causeway.
"The operation aims to safeguard public security and ensure smooth movement and activities throughout the festive period," he said during a visit to the Deepavali bazaar in Jalan Trus today.
Rahaman said police expected heavier traffic on major routes, particularly along both directions of the North-South Expressway in Johor.
He advised motorists to obey traffic regulations, plan their journeys early and avoid driving when tired or under the influence of alcohol.
Meanwhile, he advised those returning to their hometowns or going on holiday to register their travel details through the Volunteer Smartphone Patrol (VSP) application.
He said the information would help police identify vacant homes and plan more effective crime prevention patrols.
Johor police recorded 5,294 registrations through the VSP application between January and October this year, compared with 4,425 during the corresponding period last year.
The increase of 869 registrations represented a rise of nearly 20 per cent.
Those without the VSP application can also register their 'balik kampung' details by completing forms available at their nearest police stations.

Title: Zahid heads to Turkiye tomorrow for TRT World Forum [WATCH]
Article:
ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will begin a working visit to Turkiye tomorrow in conjunction with the 2026 TRT World Forum, scheduled for Nov 6 and 7.
Malaysian ambassador to Turkiye Adlan Mohd Shaffieq said the visit, which runs until Nov 8, would include a meeting with Turkish Vice-President Cevdet Yilmaz.
"The deputy prime minister will take part as a panellist at the forum, which Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan will officiate.
"Zahid will also meet his counterpart from Lebanon, Tarek Mitri, at the Istanbul Convention Centre, where the TRT World Forum will be held," he said at a press conference in conjunction with Zahid's visit today.
Zahid will deliver a speech at the forum in a session titled "Turkiye, From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor", which focuses on Turkiye's role in the geopolitical landscape and its ties to regional and international developments.
The TRT World Forum is an international platform that brings together political leaders, policymakers, academics and civil society representatives to discuss global issues and approaches to shared challenges.
Malaysian figures who have previously participated in the forum include Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 2018 and 2019, former international trade and industry minister Tan Sri Rafidah Aziz in 2019, and public health expert Professor Dr Jemilah Mahmood in 2020.
Meanwhile, Adlan said Zahid would attend a roundtable with the Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research (Seta), a leading Turkish think tank specialising in foreign and security policy, on Saturday.
He said the engagement would follow up on the memorandum of understanding signed between Seta and the Institute of Strategic and International Studies Malaysia during Anwar's visit to Turkiye in January.
"This meeting will build on that agreement, with discussions expected to focus on geo-economics and geopolitics, particularly current developments," he said.
Adlan said Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, is scheduled to witness the signing of letters of collaboration (LoCs) between Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) and Sabanci University and Yildiz Technical University, which 17 Mara-sponsored students will also attend.
"The main focus of these LoCs is to promote technical and vocational education and training (TVET). This is a very positive development.
"Turkiye's Higher Education Minister Yusuf Tekin, who also oversees TVET in the country, will pay a courtesy call on the deputy prime minister," he said.
Malaysia and Turkiye established diplomatic relations on June 17, 1964, and have since maintained close ties in various fields, including politics, economy, trade and education.
Bilateral trade between the two countries now stands at US$5.6 billion, with Anwar and Erdogan agreeing in January to raise it to US$10 billion by 2030.
Malaysia is Turkiye's largest trading partner in Southeast Asia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kee Ming lands RM44.2mil data centre job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kee Ming Group Bhd's unit Kee Ming Electrical Sdn Bhd has received a contract for electrical work at a hyperscale data centre in Puncak Alam worth RM44.17 million.
The company said a third-party contractor specialising in integrated mechanical and electrical solutions awarded the contract.
Kee Ming Electrical will undertake the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of general electrical works, which will commence upon acceptance of the letter of award.
Meanwhile the electrical works for the main building will commence upon the issuance of a notice to proceed by the contractor.
The subcontract works are expected to be completed by July 30, 2027.
"As data centre developments require reliable and sophisticated electrical infrastructure, we believe our experience in delivering integrated electrical engineering solutions positions us well to participate in this growing sector," said Kee Ming managing director Liew Kar Hoe.
He added the latest project further strengthens the group's data centre project portfolio and reinforces its strategy of pursuing higher-value engineering opportunities.
"Moving forward, we remain focused on delivering our existing projects efficiently while actively pursuing new opportunities across data centres, high-voltage and interconnection facilities, as well as industrial and commercial developments."
As at June 30, Kee Ming's outstanding order book stood at RM206.40 million.
Since its listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on Feb 12, Kee Ming has announced six project wins with an aggregate value of RM182.23 million.

Title: Building grit, not fragility
Article:
LETTER:
Public discussions across Malaysia and the broader Asian region have increasingly focused on the coping mechanisms of young adults in the modern workplace.
The term "Strawberry Generation", which was popularised to describe youth perceived as easily bruised by minor pressures, has resurfaced as seasoned professionals, community leaders, and religious figures voice growing concern over a perceived decline in psychological endurance.
The root of this fragility often begins long before a young adult enters the workforce.
Many point directly to modern parenting dynamics, where excessive indulgence, reluctance to enforce discipline, and a desire to shield children from every discomfort have inadvertently nurtured fragility.
This poses a complex challenge for Asian societies, including Malaysia, as institutions navigate the transition between traditional work ethics and contemporary workplace wellness standards.
Historically, Asian educational and family structures emphasised endurance, deference to authority and perseverance through adversity.
Today, increased global interconnectedness and heightened awareness of psychological well-being have prompted a welcome shift toward prioritising mental health in schools, universities, and corporate environments.
However, a critical distinction must be maintained between supporting genuine mental health needs and conflating everyday hardship with medical crises.
Resilience is not developed in environments completely devoid of friction.
It is forged through navigating structured challenges and learning to adapt when primary plans fail.
For Malaysia's developing workforce, addressing this issue requires a balanced approach.
Organisations and educational institutions must continue to destigmatise mental health conditions and provide structured support systems for those in genuine distress.
At the same time, workplace culture and family foundations must reinforce emotional fortitude, self-reliance, and problem-solving capabilities.
Young professionals must be encouraged to view struggle not as an unnatural imposition, but as a standard driver of personal and professional development.
Cultivating psychological toughness alongside compassion is essential for long-term growth.
Encourage young individuals to build fortitude rather than retreat from routine friction.
Ultimately, we can foster a resilient generation capable of sustaining both individual well-being and collective progress.
AHMAD FAIZUDDIN
School of Education and Liberal Arts
INTI International University, Malaysia
DR FAHAINIS MOHD YUSUF
School of Education
Universiti Utara Malaysia
