Title: 35 foreigners nabbed in Bayan Lepas online love, gold investment scam raids
Article:
BALIK PULAU: Police have arrested 35 foreigners suspected of operating an online love and gold investment scam syndicate during raids in Bayan Lepas.
Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said the operation was conducted about 2.10pm on Nov 2 by the district Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID), together with the Penang contingent CCID.
He said the raids targeted two residential premises in Bayan Lepas.
"Those detained comprise 33 Chinese national men, one Chinese woman and one Taiwanese man," he said in a statement today.
He said initial investigations revealed that the syndicate had been operating since September 2026, targeting Chinese national women aged between 18 and 46 through Telegram.
"Police seized 119 mobile phones and three laptops, along with chargers, estimated to be worth RM60,000. The items are believed to have been used in the illicit operations," he added.
The case is being investigated under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code for cheating and criminal conspiracy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sunway debuts at 26th in Fortune 100 regional workplace ranking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Group debuted at the 26th spot on the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For Southeast Asia 2026 list.
It became the only Malaysian-headquartered company among the 100 organisations recognised across the region.
Produced by Fortune and Great Place To Work, the ranking draws on confidential feedback from more than 1.32 million employees across 10 Southeast Asian countries.
"While business performance is important, it is ultimately people and values that define the strength and longevity of an organisation.
"We are humbled to be recognised among Southeast Asia's best workplaces. It reaffirms our commitment to building a workplace where people can flourish and do their best work.
"Our journey over the years has been built on trust, guided by our core values of integrity, humility and excellence.
"These qualities will continue to guide our path as we grow alongside the communities we serve, and create opportunities for generations to come,"said Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah.
To qualify, companies must be Great Place To Work Certified and employ at least 200 people in the region.
Employees assess their workplace through 60 statements and two open-ended questions covering trust, leadership, respect, fairness and pride. Surveys must also meet distribution and response-rate thresholds to ensure a representative sample.
Beyond overall scores, the assessment evaluates how consistently positive experiences are shared across roles, seniority levels and demographic groups.
Rankings also take into account regional workforce size and the number of countries in which companies are certified and surveyed.
According to Great Place To Work's published profile, 93 per cent of surveyed employees regard Sunway as a great place to work.
The workplace recognition is one of three Fortune accolades involving Sunway this year.
The group climbed 39 places to No. 151 on the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 companies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM805.2mil allocated to six less-developed states under 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Economy Ministry has allocated RM805.2 million, or 67.8 per cent of its development expenditure, to six less-developed states under the 2027 Budget to narrow regional development gaps.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the allocation would stimulate economic opportunities and promote more balanced growth across the country.
The six states are Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis, Sabah, Sarawak and Terengganu.
He said the ministry also allocated RM813.8 million, or 38.4 per cent of its development expenditure, for programmes and projects directly benefiting the people.
"Priority is given to community infrastructure development, income-generating opportunities, human capital development and entrepreneurship, as well as business opportunities and economic mobility," he said.
He was winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the committee stage in the Dewan Rakyat.
Akmal Nasrullah said the ministry was allocated RM645.44 million for operating expenditure and RM2.12 billion for development expenditure under the 2027 Budget.
He said development expenditure increased by 11.9 per cent compared with 2026, covering 131 projects comprising 41 new projects and 90 ongoing projects.
Of these, 41 projects would be implemented across four economic corridor regions, including five new projects and 36 ongoing projects.
The Northern Corridor Implementation Authority would oversee 18 projects worth RM193.6 million, while the East Coast Economic Region Development Council would implement 13 projects worth RM214.8 million.
The Regional Corridor Development Authority would implement six projects worth RM201 million, while the Sabah Economic Development and Investment Authority would oversee four projects worth RM170.4 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy awards Melania Trump state honour
Article:
KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has awarded US first lady Melania Trump a state honour for her role in helping to organise a humanitarian evacuation from a frontline town last week, according to a decree published on Wednesday.
The presidential decree, dated Nov 2, cited her "significant personal contribution" to humanitarian support for Ukraine and her work to help Ukrainian children, including those deported or forcibly moved from Russian-occupied territory.
The award - the Order of Princess Olga, 1st class - honours women who have made exceptional contributions in spheres including science, education, culture and charitable work.
Ukrainian officials have said Melania played a pivotal role in organising the six-day ceasefire to evacuate civilians from the Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian town of Oleshky, which concluded on Sunday.
It was the longest local pause in fighting since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
Nearly 800 people were evacuated, Melania said.
Meanwhile, the US First Lady will host "representatives" of Russia and Ukraine in Washington, the White House said Tuesday, without giving a date or saying who may attend.
The meeting between parties from the two warring countries will take place at the White House and represents an "extraordinary moment in American history," the statement said.
On Thursday, Melania will also make a statement on a recent four day-long truce in southern Kherson region, the White House said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Finance Ministry: Price of RON97 down by 20 sen, RON95 and diesel drop by 15 sen respectively tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The retail price of RON97 has dropped by 20 sen to RM4.70 per liter, while unsubsidised RON95 and diesel have both dropped 15 sen to RM4.27 and RM5.12 per liter respectively for the period of November 5 to 11.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF), in a statement today, announced that this pricing is determined based on the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) formula, compared to the current prices of RM4.90 for RON97, RM4.42 for unsubsidised RON95, and RM5.27 for unsubsidised diesel.
“The regional petroleum market shows signs of moderation following an increase in the supply of refined fuels, including petrol and diesel stocks in Singapore, which serves as one of the market references for petroleum pricing in Malaysia.
“This development, together with the drop in Brent crude oil prices at the end of the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period, indicates the possibility of lower price pressures,” according to the statement.
However, MOF noted that geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia continue to pose risks to world petroleum price stability.
Meanwhile, the price of subsidised RON95 through Budi95 remains at RM1.99 per liter, with the government bearing a subsidy of RM2.28 per liter, or 53 percent of the unsubsidised price for the period.
For Budi Diesel, the price for eligible recipients remains at RM2.10 per liter, involving a government subsidy of RM3.02 per liter, or 59 percent of the unsubsidised price.
Additionally, the price of petrol under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) remains at RM2.05 per liter, while diesel under the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) remains at RM2.15 per liter.
According to the MOF, eligible Malaysians can continue to purchase subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad, subject to monthly eligibility limits.
“The Madani Government will continue to take a prudent approach to protect the rakyat from price fluctuations, while ensuring that the country’s fuel supply remains adequate and secure,” the statement added. — Bernama

Title: Penang e-hailing drivers to get one-off RM600 aid from 2027
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — A one-off payment of RM600 for e-hailing drivers in Penang will be disbursed in 2027, with applications opening in January 2027 through the i-Sejahtera system.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the application criteria for the Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance would be announced next month.
“E-hailing services have become an important component of the urban transport system, supporting first- and last-mile connectivity while providing the public with flexible mobility services.
“In line with the Unity Manifesto that was announced, a payment of RM600 will be disbursed in 2027, with applications to be submitted through the i-Sejahtera system,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates (State Budget 2027) at the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, when tabling the 2027 State Budget on Friday (Oct 30), announced that the state government would introduce a one-off Special E-Hailing Incentive Assistance of RM600 for eligible drivers, with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million.
In a separate development, Zairil said the state government had submitted an application to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for RM750 million in funding under the Universal Service Provision (USP) Fund to implement the Communication Infrastructure and Digital Connectivity for Penang Smart City initiative.
He said the proposed initiative included the development of about 290 kilometres of fibre-optic network, mainly in Seberang Perai, the expansion of last-mile facilities and communication tower infrastructure and connectivity support for private 5G networks.
He said it would also involve the development of a Network Operations Centre (NOC), artificial intelligence (AI)-based smart asset monitoring and provision of high-speed public WiFi facilities to strengthen the state’s overall digital capabilities.
“As such, the state government hopes that MCMC will give due consideration to and subsequently approve this application for funding to enable the initiative to be implemented in Penang.
“Approval of the allocation will serve as a catalyst for the development of more integrated and resilient digital infrastructure, thus enhancing the state’s capacity to navigate technological advancements,” he added.
The State Legislative Assembly sitting will resume tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Mutiara Line LRT link to Penang Sentral to begin construction in 2027, completion targeted for 2031
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Construction of the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) alignment linking Macallum on the island to Penang Sentral in Seberang Perai, including a marine bridge across the Penang Strait, is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027.
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the tender evaluation process for the alignment was currently being undertaken by MRT Corp, the implementing agency, and was expected to be completed this month.
“Construction is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027, following the appointment of the main contractor for the Macallum-Penang Sentral alignment. Preliminary works will be carried out first, followed by major construction activities, including the construction of a bridge across the Penang Strait.
“The alignment is targeted for completion by December 2031, in tandem with the section linking Silicon Island to Komtar on the island,” he said in a written reply during the State Assembly sitting here today.
He was responding to a question from Kumaran Krishnan (PH-Bagan Dalam) on the commencement of the LRT alignment in Seberang Perai, particularly the section leading to Penang Sentral.
Zairil said the finalised Macallum-Penang Sentral alignment would feature a 5.5-kilometre (km) marine bridge across the Penang Strait, with two main stations at Macallum and Penang Sentral.
The Bagan Luar station, meanwhile, has been designated as a provisional station to facilitate possible future expansion of the alignment.
The Mutiara Line LRT project is scheduled to begin construction in 2025, with operations expected to commence in December 2031. The line will span approximately 29.67 km and comprise 20 stations, in addition to two provisional stations.
As the first integrated metro transit system in the northern region, the project is expected to improve connectivity between Penang Island and the mainland, ease traffic congestion and enhance accessibility. — Bernama

Title: In Johor, six-year-old boy drowns after falling into reservoir while fishing
Article:
KULAI, Nov 4 — A six-year-old boy drowned after falling into a reservoir while fishing at Jalan Budiman in Kampung Melayu Kulai here today.
Kulai Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Awang Adzwan Awang Sahari said authorities received a distress call on the incident at 10.17am.
He said six personnel, assisted by an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit, were immediately dispatched to the scene that was located four kilometres from the fire station.
“Upon arrival, the responding team discovered that a boy had fallen into the reservoir and was believed to have drowned,” he said in a statement today.
Awang Adzwan said the team located the victim and carried out a rescue operation.
He said the team employed the use of ropes and a stretcher to retrieve the victim from the reservoir.
The victim, who is a Primary One pupil, was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical assistant.
The operation concluded at 11.25am.

Title: Over five million Malaysians to receive RM1.1b STR aid from today, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The fourth phase of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid, amounting to RM1.1 billion, is being disbursed starting today to over five million recipients nationwide, as part of ongoing efforts to assist the public in coping with the pressure of the cost of living.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the disbursement is being made in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration and covers recipients from various ethnic backgrounds.
He noted that this assistance reflects the government's commitment to ensuring that the welfare of the people particularly those in the low-income group remains a priority.
“Therefore, in conjunction with Deepavali, I am announcing that from today until November 6, a total of RM1.1 billion in STR aid will be distributed to more than five million people,” he said while speaking during a visit to the Deepavali Mega Bazaar 2026 in Brickfields here today.
Also present were Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and Minister of Digital Gobind Singh Deo. — Bernama

Title: Selangor gears up for north-east monsoon, deploys 7,677 personnel for disaster response
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 4 — The Selangor state government has mobilised 7,677 personnel from various state agencies to prepare for disasters during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to continue until March 2027.
State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the mobilisation involved the State Disaster Management Unit (UPBN), local authorities, district offices and relevant agencies to coordinate operations and monitor high-risk areas.
In a statement today, she said the operation was supported by 708 land vehicles, 247 water transport assets and various rescue equipment, including 5,739 tents, 1,950 life jackets, 141 water pumps and 20 drones.
According to the Selangor Drainage and Irrigation Department (JPS), the state is expected to receive 2,232 millimetres of rainfall this year, with 1,460 mm, or 65 per cent, recorded as at November 1. Rainfall of 268 mm and 230 mm is forecast for November and December respectively.
Jamaliah said JPS was monitoring flood risks through 221 rainfall telemetry stations, 124 water-level monitoring stations, 140 warning sirens and 72 IP cameras.
Based on 2025 data, JPS had identified 56 flood hotspots and 232 flood-prone areas, with Klang recording the highest number of hotspots at 13, followed by Petaling (11), Gombak (10) and Hulu Langat (nine).
She also cautioned residents in coastal and river estuary areas of Klang, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Langat, Sabak Bernam and Kuala Selangor about the risk of high tides.
Meanwhile, 1,161 temporary relief centres (PPS) had been identified statewide, including 696 schools under the Education Ministry, 242 public halls and 135 community halls.
Jamaliah said agencies had been instructed to ensure the centres were safe, equipped with basic facilities and sufficient food supplies, while giving due attention to vulnerable groups.
She advised residents to monitor weather alerts through the JPS Public InfoBanjir portal and the Malaysian Meteorological Department’s (MET Malaysia) myCuaca 3.0 application, and comply with evacuation orders. — Bernama

Title: Klang Valley raids uncover suspected luxury liquor tax-stamp scam, RM702,566 haul seized
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Police have uncovered a suspected tax-stamp diversion scheme involving luxury liquor following the seizure of 370 bottles worth RM702,566 in the Klang Valley on Monday and yesterday.
The operation, Ops Taring Alpha 2, was conducted by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) of the Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA), in collaboration with the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Customs Department.
WCB/PSK commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the liquor, packed in 73 boxes, was seized during separate raids at a warehouse in Selangor and business premises in the capital.
He said initial inspections at the warehouse found that some luxury liquor bottles allegedly bore tax stamps or customs labels with lower duty rates than those applicable to the products.
“The modus operandi is believed to involve the diversion of tax stamps to evade excise duty payments, potentially resulting in revenue leakage,” he said in a statement today.
However, inspections at the second premises found that all liquor bottles bore valid tax stamps, with no offences detected.
Mohd Zaki said four individuals, including three Bangladeshis, were arrested to assist investigations under Section 15(1)(c) and Section 55B of the Immigration Act 1959/63, as well as Regulation 39(B) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
The Customs Department is also investigating possible offences under Section 133(1)(c) of the Customs Act 1967. — Bernama

Title: Three boat operators among 38 Indonesians held in Selangor migrant smuggling crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Three boat operators were among 38 Indonesian nationals detained by the General Operations Force (GOF) in an operation to curb migrant smuggling along the coastal area of Kampung Sungai Gatal, near Sabak Bernam, on November 2.
GOF Central Brigade acting commander ACP Awang Arfian Awang Bujang said all of them were detained in a raid under Op Taring Delta at about 4.30am while they were believed to be attempting to leave Malaysia via an illegal sea route.
He said the other 35 individuals arrested comprised 24 adult men and 11 adult women.
“The operations team also seized a fishing boat, a Mitsubishi engine and three mobile phones of various brands, which are believed to have been used as communication devices in the smuggling operation.
“The total value of the seizures is estimated at RM406,800,” he told a press conference here today.
He said the case was being investigated under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM) and the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Awang Arfian said the GOF Central Brigade recorded 171 cases involving migrant smuggling activities and immigration offences from January 1 to November 4 this year.
He said enforcement operations during the period led to the arrest of 898 individuals in the brigade’s area of responsibility, which covers Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor.
“Of the total, 33 cases were investigated under ATIPSOM, involving the arrest of 76 boat operators, while another 138 cases were recorded under the Immigration Act 1959/63, with 822 arrests,” he said.
He said the GOF would continue to intensify operations and intelligence gathering to combat migrant smuggling and other illegal cross-border activities.
“Members of the public with information on such activities are urged to channel it to the police for further action,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says aid for Indian community goes beyond Mitra, more initiatives in pipeline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Government assistance for the Indian community is not only channelled through the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), but also includes various initiatives in welfare, entrepreneurship, education and social development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said such assistance was also provided through various government agencies and programmes, including the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid scheme, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), entrepreneurship financing through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, as well as allocations for the development of Tamil schools and places of worship.
“Sometimes, people think that the only assistance available for the Indian community is MITRA, whereas there are also STR, Amanah Ikhtiar, and Tekun (Nasional)... all of these are also part of the support we provide.
“Is this enough? Not yet. That I agree, but we are gradually increasing. We are discussing this constructively to introduce new initiatives where there were none before,” he said during a visit to the Brickfields Deepavali Mega Bazaar 2026 here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Anwar, also the Finance Minister, said Mitra’s annual allocation, which has stood at RM100 million since 2008, has been increased to RM150 million, which is a 50 per cent rise.
He said priority would be given to skills training programmes and employment opportunities for young members of the Indian community, particularly in industrial automation, technology and aircraft maintenance.
The government is also expanding financing facilities through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, with an additional RM150 million allocated to assist entrepreneurs from the Indian community.
In the education sector, Anwar said the allocation for repair and maintenance works at Tamil National-Type Schools (SJKT) had been increased to RM50 million, with priority given to dilapidated schools and those requiring urgent attention.
He said the government also planned to fully rebuild SJKT Ladang Pamol in Kluang, Johor, as well as establish six new SJKTs, including in Sungai Bakap, Penang and Klebang, Perak.
Meanwhile, the allocation for the maintenance and development of registered places of worship was also increased to RM80 million next year, compared with RM50 million annually since 2021.
“This form of assistance existed previously, but under the Madani Government, it has been increased in stages following discussions and assessments of the community’s needs,” Anwar added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian prosecutors unable to find Yusoff Rawther in UK to physically serve appeal notice despite Interpol help
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — The Court of Appeal was told today that the prosecution has yet to physically serve a notice of appeal on Muhammed Yusoff Rawther, a former research assistant to a politician, who is currently in the United Kingdom (UK).
Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) How May Ling told a three-member panel that authorities in the UK and Ireland had failed to locate Muhammed Yusoff or serve the notice on him, despite assistance being sought from Interpol.
“The prosecution was informed last month that efforts to locate the respondent (Muhammed Yusoff) had been unsuccessful. The authorities also had no information regarding his asylum application,” she said during case management before Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and K. Muniandy.
The prosecution is appealing against the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision to acquit and discharge Muhammed Yusoff of charges of trafficking cannabis and possessing two imitation pistols at the end of the prosecution’s case, without calling him to enter his defence.
How said the respondent’s counsel had informed the court during an earlier proceeding that they were still in contact with him and had received instructions to represent him in the appeal.
The DPP said the prosecution was seeking another case management date to allow efforts to locate Muhammed Yusoff and serve the notice to continue.
It also applied for the proceedings to be conducted via Zoom so that he could appear online and confirm his whereabouts in the UK, facilitating service of the appeal notice.
On the Zoom application, Justice Azman said the case should not be treated differently from other criminal cases.
“I do not want to make an exception in this case. This is a criminal proceeding, and the respondent must appear physically in court. This court also does not want to set an unnecessary precedent.
“If the prosecution succeeds in locating him, bring him before this court,” he said.
Justice Azman also urged the lawyer to advise his client to return to Malaysia, given that they had a channel of communication with him.
Counsel Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, representing Muhammed Yusoff, said he acknowledged that physical service of the appeal notice was a legal requirement under Section 314 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
However, he maintained that his client was not on the run but was in the UK to seek asylum.
The court fixed February 3 next year for further case management.
On June 12, 2025, High Court Judge Datuk Muhammad Jamil Hussin acquitted and discharged Muhammed Yusoff, 33, after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him.
The court found that the prosecution had failed to prove, through witness testimony, that the accused had control, custody or possession of the two pistols and the drugs.
Muhammed Yusoff was charged with trafficking 305 grammes of cannabis found in a vehicle he was travelling in outside the surau at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters at 10.15am on September 6, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, which provides for life imprisonment and not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction.
He was also charged with possessing two imitation pistols by the roadside near a condominium in Jalan Bukit Kiara at 9.25am on the same day.
The charge was under Section 36(1) of the Arms Act 1960, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM5,000, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Penang DOSH to probe cause of fatal Paya Terubong landslide, developer told to submit documents
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is conducting an investigation to determine the actual cause of the landslide at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, covering aspects such as safety, construction, and regulatory compliance.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said the investigation includes gathering information and statements from the developer, contractors, and consultants involved in the development project on the slope near the site of the incident.
“The Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) held discussions yesterday (Nov 3) with civil and geotechnical consulting engineers, the developer, and the contractor to investigate and understand the root cause of the incident covering aspects of safety, construction, design, and compliance with relevant regulations as well as to propose appropriate mitigation measures and site stabilization efforts.
“DOSH has requested that the developer submit Pre-Construction Information (PCI) documentation before commencing any mitigation work on-site,” he said when winding the debate on the Supply Bill and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates (State Budget 2027) at the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
In the incident on October 25, a doctor, Dr Wong Kar Lin, 73, died after being buried in a landslide that affected his home, while his wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim (in her 80s), managed to escape safely.
Elaborating further, H’ng said the approved 35-story affordable housing project near the site does not exceed the 76-metre (250-foot) contour line while infrastructure development such as roads and utilities is permitted, subject to strict conditions outlined in the geotechnical report approved by the Committee for Development on Risky Land on April 10, 2023.
Additionally, he explained that the development approval for the site dates back to 1996, when the initial developer submitted an application for a proposed project consisting of medium-cost apartments and townhouses.
The planning permission application subsequently underwent several changes in terms of the developer and the proposed development plan before... The application for planning permission for the development of the affordable housing project was submitted in 2023.
“I wish to emphasise here that all decisions made were collective decisions of the government not merely the decision of the Chief Minister, but rather those of the State Authority and the Local Authority,” he stated.
In response to a query from Muhammad Fauzi Yusoff (PN-Sungai Dua), who interjected to urge the establishment of a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) to investigate the cause of the tragedy, H’ng said the state government would first defer the investigation process to the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) before considering such a measure.
He explained that the relevant documentation must be examined by DOSH, with technical advice sought from the Engineering Department of the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) specifically regarding geotechnical aspects to ensure that the proposed mitigation works are appropriate, before any further action is taken.
Previously, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow asserted that the landowner and the developer of the condominium project must be held accountable, including regarding legal implications and the implementation of mitigation works to ensure the safety of the area affected by the landslide. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest 35 foreigners in Penang love scam, gold investment fraud raids
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Police arrested 35 foreign nationals suspected of involvement in an online fraud syndicate specialising in love scams and gold investment schemes during raids on two residences in Bayan Lepas, near here, last Monday.
Barat Daya police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said the suspects, comprising 33 Chinese men, one Chinese woman and one Taiwanese man, were arrested in an operation conducted by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division in collaboration with the Penang Contingent Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID).
“Preliminary investigations revealed that the syndicate began operating last September, targeting Chinese national women aged between 18 and 46 through the Telegram application,” he said in a statement today.
He said police also seized 119 mobile phones, three laptops and chargers, believed to have been used to facilitate the syndicate’s activities, with the total estimated value of the seized items amounting to RM60,000.
All the suspects are on remand to assist in investigations under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code.
In another development, Anuwal said police were conducting further investigations into an accident involving a Rapid Penang bus and a motorcycle along Jalan Mayang Pasir, near here, last night, which claimed the life of a 29-year-old motorcyclist.
He said police were recording witness statements, reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and examining the vehicles involved to assist in investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, relating to causing death by reckless or dangerous driving. — Bernama

Title: HR minister: 864 employers, including VVIPs, MPs and assemblymen, fail to pay Socso for domestic workers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — A total of 864 high-profile individuals, including prominent figures (VVIPs), members of parliament and state assemblymen, have been identified for failing to pay Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for their domestic workers.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the figure was part of 10,033 employers of domestic workers found to have failed to comply with the contribution requirements, based on Perkeso’s preliminary checks as at November 1.
Asked whether any ministers were among the employers who had failed to comply, Ramanan revealed that individuals holding positions higher than Cabinet members had also been found to have committed the offence.
“Some are even higher-ranking than ministers. The 864 high-profile individuals include those holding key positions in the public and private sectors, as well as prominent figures, members of parliament, state assemblymen and other employers of domestic workers.
“The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) views any failure to register domestic workers and pay their Perkeso contributions seriously,” he told a press conference after the presentation of Perkeso benefits to victims of the Nepal floods at Menara Perkeso here today.
Also present were Perkeso Board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal and Perkeso Group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.
Ramanan said all employers concerned, including VVIPs, had been given until December 7 to fulfil their contribution obligations, failing which action would be taken against them.
He said enforcement would begin with the issuance of compounds, while employers who continued to disregard the requirements could face a fine of up to RM10,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both.
“We do not want to embarrass anyone. Please check whether you have paid or not. If you have, thank you. If you have not, please pay. No one is above the law. The law applies to everyone without exception.
“We cannot talk about workers’ welfare and rights if we fail to fulfil even the most basic responsibilities towards the workers in our own homes. Leadership by example must begin with compliance with the law,” he said.
Ramanan also disclosed that another 26,669 employers had been identified as having outstanding contribution records, which required further checks and follow-up action by Perkeso.
He said he had instructed Perkeso to take a firm stance in strengthening monitoring and enforcement against employers who failed to fulfil their responsibilities, adding that the main objective was not to impose compounds or fines, but to ensure that domestic workers received the social security protection they were entitled to. — Bernama
Socso is the English name for Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (Perkeso), Malaysia’s Social Security Organisation.

Title: Sungai Buloh floods leave 306 people at three evacuation centres
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — A total of 306 victims from 59 families are still taking shelter at three temporary evacuation centres (PPS) in Sungai Buloh as of 2pm today following floods that hit their homes early this morning.
Sungai Buloh District Police Chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said all the affected victims are from Kampung Kubu Gajah, Kampung Merbau Sempak, Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir, Kampung Paya Jaras Dalam, and the Selangor State Development Corporation (PKNS) Low-Cost Housing.
He said all the victims have been placed at three PPS: the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) Dewan Seri Pagi, Sekolah Kebangsaan Merbau Sempak in Sungai Buloh, and Dewan Siantan in Kampung Melayu Subang.
“The Sungai Buloh District Police Headquarters (IPD) received 356 police reports from victims affected by the flood incident as of 2pm.
“The flood incident also caused damage to the riverbank near the bridge on Jalan Utama Kampung Kubu Gajah, affecting its structural stability before the bridge eventually collapsed,” he said in a statement here today.
Mohd Hafiz said following the incident, the main route connecting Kampung Kubu Gajah and Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir has been fully closed for safety reasons.
He noted that the Petaling District Public Works Department (JKR) has provided alternative routes via Jalan Merbau Sempak from Federal Route 54 (FT54) to Kampung Kubu Gajah, as well as Jalan Paya Jaras Hilir from FT54 to Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir.
“Repair works for the damaged riverbank are estimated to take between two to three weeks,” he said.
He also advised the public to remain vigilant, comply with authorities’ instructions, use the designated alternative routes, avoid risky areas, and obtain up-to-date and authentic information due to the ongoing North-east Monsoon phenomenon. — Bernama

Title: Google commits additional US$15b to Malaysia data centre expansion over two years, projects 37,000 jobs as Anwar hails investment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Google will invest an additional US$15 billion (RM61 billion) in Malaysia over the next two years to expand its data centre infrastructure, which is expected to contribute an annual average of US$1.1 billion to the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).
Alphabet and Google president and chief investment officer Ruth Porat said the investment would cover the expansion of Google’s existing data centre campus at Elmina Business Park in Selangor, as well as new planned campuses in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan.
“We are very excited about expanding our digital infrastructure here responsibly, investing in resource stewardship, clean energy initiatives, as well as new skilling programmes in order to open pathways to economic opportunity for Malaysians across the country,” she said at the Mantap Malaysia Bersama AI at Universiti Malaya here.
She said the construction phase, scheduled for 2027 and 2028, was expected to support more than 37,000 local jobs annually and generate an average annual labour income of US$378 million.
Once operational, the facilities are projected to support more than 9,000 long-term local jobs, with average wages 45 per cent above Malaysia’s median wage.
Porat said the investment reflected Google’s confidence in Malaysia’s leadership, skilled workforce and commitment to digital transformation, while strengthening the company’s presence in the country and Southeast Asia.
She added that Google was working with more than 80 Malaysian entities across sectors including civil engineering, power systems, network infrastructure and logistics to develop and operate its facilities.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who witnessed the announcement, described the investment as a major milestone in Malaysia’s efforts to become a leading digital powerhouse in South-east Asia.
He said foreign direct investment was indispensable to the country’s economic development, but its benefits should extend beyond capital inflows and infrastructure to strengthen local businesses, develop human capital and ensure responsible management of natural resources.
“What is especially gratifying is how Google has chosen to work with our domestic private sector, universities and research centres,” he said.
Anwar said Google’s partnerships with more than 80 Malaysian entities demonstrated the capabilities of local companies to participate in major international projects and strengthen their competitiveness.
He also welcomed Google’s commitment to upskill 800,000 Malaysians by 2031 through four programmes targeting educators and students, microentrepreneurs, local council officers and vocational jobseekers.
On energy, Anwar said Google would work with Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) to add more than 1 gigawatt of clean energy capacity to the national grid without relying on public subsidies.
He also highlighted Google’s water stewardship initiatives, including plans to develop an off-river storage reservoir and water treatment plant in Negeri Sembilan, which are expected to supply 65 million litres of treated water daily.
Anwar said the facility would help mitigate flood risks during the monsoon season, secure water reserves during dry periods and strengthen water supply, with ownership to be handed over to the state government upon completion.
When asked by reporters if Google had done enough for environmental concerns, Anwar briefly said “yes, these are the conditions imposed and they’ve accepted it.”
Google said the US$15 billion investment builds on its more than 15-year presence in Malaysia and expands on its digital infrastructure investment announced in 2024.
Google had previously announced a US$2 billion investment in Malaysia in May 2024, including the development of its first data centre and Google Cloud region in the country, both based in Elmina Business Park, Selangor.

Title: Ramanan: Socso to pay RM174,000 in benefits to families of 28 Nepal-Tibet flood victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Twenty-eight out of the 54 victims of the flood tragedy in the Nepal-Tibet region on August 26 met the contribution eligibility requirements of Social Security Organisation (Socso), thereby entitling their next-of-kin to receive benefits.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the total payout, amounting to RM174,000, includes an immediate financial aid of RM3,000 as well as a Survivors’ Pension under the Invalidity Scheme, which has been disbursed to the families of the affected victims.
“Today, 16 families (out of the 28 eligible families) are present. I understand that, to this day, these families continue to face uncertainty regarding the fate of their loved ones. I am well aware that no form of assistance can truly alleviate such deep anxiety.
“Nevertheless, on behalf of the government, I do not want these families especially those who have lost their primary breadwinner to bear this burden alone. Therefore, the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma), through Socso, has strived to ensure that the eligible next-of-kin receive appropriate protection and support,” he said.
He made these remarks during a press conference held today at the PERKESO Tower in Kuala Lumpur, regarding the disbursement of Socso benefits to the victims of the Nepal floods. Also present were Socso board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal and Socso group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr. Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.
Ramanan noted that Socso has conducted a thorough review to ensure that no eligible next-of-kin is overlooked or excluded from receiving the necessary protection.
“The pension disbursement process will be carried out as soon as all relevant information and documentation are complete. For victims who do not have a record of Socso contributions, please know that we remain deeply concerned and attentive to the plight of your families.”
“Through the Social Synergy Programme, Socso will help connect affected families with 990 strategic partners including 130 agencies nationwide to identify other suitable forms of assistance to help ease their burden,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Tengku Zafrul says Malaysia’s RM431.1b approved investments reflect investor confidence as country courts new partnerships
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Malaysia highlighted opportunities for cooperation in the semiconductor, artificial intelligence (AI), digital infrastructure, clean energy and halal industries at the B57+ Business Leaders’ Summit 2026 in Istanbul, Türkiye.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said these sectors were among the potential areas for further exploration to strengthen economic cooperation between Malaysia and other countries.
He said Malaysia also offered its strategic position as a gateway to the ASEAN market to international investors.
In a post on the X platform, he said the matters were discussed during his participation in a panel session at the summit, which also addressed the role of sovereign wealth funds in strengthening economic cooperation among developing countries.
Tengku Zafrul also highlighted Malaysia’s investment performance, which recorded RM431.1 billion in approved investments in 2025 and RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026.
He added that 87 per cent of the 5,822 manufacturing projects approved between 2021 and June 2026 had reached various stages of implementation.
“These figures reflect investors’ confidence in Malaysia, but our work does not stop at attracting investments. Through MIDA, we are focused on ensuring that approved projects are actually implemented,” he said.
Tengku Zafrul said investment success should not be measured solely by the amount of investment secured, but also by the creation of quality jobs, technology transfers and opportunities generated for local companies.
“These are the benefits we want for Malaysians,” he added.
The B57+ Business Leaders’ Summit 2026 is an international business and investment summit held in Istanbul, Türkiye, on October 31 and November 1.
The summit aims to strengthen economic, trade and investment cooperation between member countries of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and their international partners. — Bernama

Title: Commuters, brace for a wet evening: MetMalaysia flags heavy storms nationwide until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a nationwide thunderstorm advisory for this evening, warning of torrential downpours, lightning, and gusty winds across Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah until 7.00pm today.
The alert, released at 3.50pm, places the entirety of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, and Perlis on high alert, alongside selected districts across several other states.
In the northern corridor, stormy weather is forecast across 11 districts in Kedah, spanning Pokok Sena, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Yan, Pendang, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu.
The warning concurrently extends across Penang’s mainland districts of Seberang Perai Utara, Tengah, and Selatan, alongside nine Perak districts, including Kerian, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Selama, and Batang Padang.
On the east coast of the peninsula, the bulletin blankets Kelantan’s interior and northern districts of Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Tanah Merah, Jeli, and Machang. In Terengganu, squalls are expected across Kemaman, Besut, Hulu Terengganu, and Dungun, while Pahang residents in Kuantan, Pekan, Maran, and Jerantut have also been advised to brace for rain. In the south, the alert spans six Johor districts, namely Tangkak, Muar, Batu Pahat, Pontian, Kluang, and Segamat.
Across East Malaysia, the advisory covers extensive divisions in Sarawak, including Sibu, Bintulu, Mukah, Sarikei, and Limbang, alongside Miri, Marudi, and Subis within the Miri division. In Sabah, stormy conditions are expected along the West Coast across Kota Belud and Ranau, before stretching into Kinabatangan and Sandakan in the Sandakan division, and Lahad Datu and Kalabakan in the Tawau division.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings whenever radar and satellite models detect rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist beyond an hour. The department noted that these bulletins serve as short-term alerts with a maximum validity of six hours from the time of issuance.
Motorists and residents across affected localities are advised to remain vigilant against localized flash floods, sudden wind squalls, and falling roadside trees or branches during the peak evening commute.

Title: Anwar says govt had previously rescued Utusan Malaysia publisher amid financial difficulties
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had previously stepped in to rescue the publisher of Utusan Malaysia and Kosmo! when the company faced operational difficulties.
As such, he said questions over the latest move to place about 100 employees on paid leave should be directed to Media Mulia Sdn Bhd, the publisher of both newspapers.
“We have rescued it once before,” he told reporters after attending the 2026 World Town Planning Day celebration and the launch of the Fifth National Physical Plan (RFN5) and Third National Urbanisation Policy (DPN3) here today.
Anwar said this when asked whether the company’s rationalisation exercise was justified and whether the affected employees would receive compensation.
On Nov 2, Media Mulia director and chief financial officer Abd Wahid Idris announced that about 100 employees would be placed under a Paid Leave Programme as part of the company’s rationalisation exercise.
He said the company was reviewing its business model, operational structure and strategic direction to ensure its long-term viability amid challenges facing the media industry. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan eyes industrial hub, jobs and investment around ECRL station in Pasir Puteh
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 4 — The development of an East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) station in Cherang Tuli, Pasir Puteh, is expected to unlock greater economic opportunities through the influx of investments, job creation, business expansion, and increased income for local residents.
Kelantan Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the state government will ensure that the area surrounding the ECRL corridor in Pasir Puteh is planned to accommodate industrial activities directly linked to the rail transport facility.
“Our focus is on processing industries, the food industry, agro-industries, warehousing, and value-added activities that can utilise the ECRL’s cargo facilities.
“This approach is crucial so that raw materials from Pasir Puteh and its surrounding areas can be processed locally before being transported to broader markets,” he said.
He was responding to a question from Nor Asilah Mohamed Zin (PAS-Limbongan) regarding the state government’s plans to ensure that Pasir Puteh derives economic benefits from the ECRL development, during the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly sitting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.
Elaborating further, Mohamed Fadzli noted that the state government has also identified the potential of developing a logistics hub, as well as a proposed dry port, in Bandar Baru Tok Bali.
He added that the provision of supporting infrastructure including road networks, warehousing areas, collection and distribution centres, and last-mile logistics facilities must be prioritised to ensure that local industry players can effectively leverage the rail transport infrastructure.
“We do not want economic opportunities to be enjoyed solely by large external corporations while the local community and local entrepreneurs must also benefit.”
“Opportunities that can be created include services in transportation, packaging, storage, maintenance, catering, and general support, as well as the supply of goods and services to the industry,” he said.
He added that the development of the industrial and logistics sector is also supported by efforts to upskill the youth in Pasir Puteh, enabling them to secure high-skilled jobs.
He noted that the employment opportunities being created are not limited to low-skilled sectors; rather, they encompass fields such as logistics, warehouse management, maintenance, technical operations, rail operations, technology, and industrial management. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan records 2,135 Syariah arrests in three years, with khalwat cases topping list
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 4 — Kelantan recorded 2,135 arrests for offences under Islamic law between 2023 and 2025, with khalwat (close proximity) offences accounting for the highest number at 1,446 cases, the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly was told today.
State Islamic Development, Dakwah, Information and Public Relations Committee chairman Mohd Asri Mat Daud said the statistics resulted from enforcement operations carried out by the Kelantan Islamic Religious Affairs Department (JAHEAIK) through its Syariah Law Enforcement Division.
He noted that 435 cases involving indecent acts or speech were also recorded, followed by 84 cases of pregnancy out of wedlock, 55 cases of exposing aurat (parts of the body required to be covered under Islamic law) in public places and 25 cases of disrespecting Ramadan.
“Another 21 cases involved men impersonating women, three involved women impersonating men, three involved encouraging immoral activities, while 63 cases were related to other miscellaneous offences.
“Of all the cases recorded, khalwat involving teenagers was the most prevalent offence during the period,” he said in reply to a question fromHafidzah Mustakim (PH-Kota Lama) on the number of arrests for Syariah offences during the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly sitting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.
Mohd Asri said Syariah law enforcement in the state is governed by the Syariah Criminal Code (I) Enactment 2019, which came into force on Nov 1, 2021, and contains 52 enforceable sections after 16 of its original 68 sections were repealed in 2024.
He said the state government remained committed to strengthening Syariah law enforcement through its Membangun Bersama Islam policy, despite various challenges, including limitations in implementing the Syariah Criminal Code.
“This year, offences involving indecent speech have also increased, warranting attention, particularly in the Kota Bharu district, which recorded 282 cases, followed by Bachok with 233 cases,” he said.
Mohd Asri said the enforcement approach focused not only on arrests and penalties but also on prevention and educating the public about compliance with the law, adding that JAHEAIK has held discussions with strategic partners, including the Royal Malaysia Police and the National Anti-Drugs Agency, to strengthen public awareness and preventive programmes.
“Briefings on Syariah law are also held regularly at state and federal government institutions, as well as educational institutions, including schools, to ensure the public understands the legal provisions in force,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina Sidek: Nearly 1,800 teachers denied permanent posts after failing key exam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4— A total of 1,799 education service officers (PPP) currently undergoing their probationary period have failed the prescribed examination for teachers, the Ministry of Education revealed in a written reply issued yesterday.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said failure in the comprehension assessment under the Mind Transformation Programme, known in Malay as
Program Transformasi Minda
(PTM) was the primary factor preventing these teachers from securing permanent service confirmation.
“As of September 30, 2026, a total of 7,723 education officers were in the process of obtaining confirmation in service, but 1,832 PPPs have yet to meet one or more established confirmation criteria,” the reply said.
The 1,799 candidates who failed the PTM assessment accounted for the overwhelming majority of those whose confirmation was delayed.
Three officers had their probationary period extended with a penalty, 29 had their probationary period extended without penalty, and one officer had their probationary status frozen.
Fadhlina said the ministry would continue to work closely with the Education Service Commission and key stakeholders to expedite unresolved confirmation cases, pledging that teacher welfare and national educational needs would remain a priority.

Title: ‘No need to go to such extremes’: Azalina tells Hadi to drop ‘Dajjal’ label in CSA criticism
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang could have found better words than “Dajjal” to voice his opposition to the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) between Bersatu MPs and the government.
The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said this when asked about Hadi’s statement yesterday, in which he likened the CSA to the Dajjal,
The Star
reported.
“There are many other words one can use to express disagreement. There is no need to go to such extremes,” she was quoted as saying after officiating a forum on Asian insolvency reform here today.
“From what I understand of the definition of the Dajjal, it is a figure who will appear towards the end of times, before the Day of Judgment.
“Does he know when the Day of Judgment will come? God knows best. I certainly do not know,” she was quoted as saying.
In Islamic belief, the Dajjal is a great deceiver whose appearance is regarded as one of the major signs that the Day of Judgment is near.
Separately, Langkawi MP Suhaimi Abdullah told the Dewan Rakyat today that the comparison was grave and harmful to national unity. Suhaimi is one of six Bersatu MPs who signed the CSA.
“How can we (as a nation) foster unity if opposition MPs are labelled ‘Dajjal’? This is unfortunate,” he said while debating Budget 2027, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported.
Suhaimi added that his children had asked him about the Dajjal.
“I said I wasn’t sure and that I was looking into it,” he reportedly said.
In his statement yesterday, Hadi said Prophet Muhammad had warned that several lesser Dajjals would appear around the world before the great Dajjal emerged, FMT reported.
“A CSA is Dajjal-like as power is no longer regarded as a trust that must be upheld for the benefit of all, but instead becomes a means of coercing others to ensure the government remains in power,” the Marang MP was quoted as saying.
Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin signed the CSA with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s government on October 29. Independent Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman also signed it.
Under the agreement, the signatories gain access to the constituency development funds that government MPs have received for the past four years, FMT reported.
In return for their support, the government commits to two reforms before the end of the parliamentary term: limiting the prime minister’s tenure and separating the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor.

Title: Hyrox Malaysia says ‘we got this wrong’, ends Carlsberg tie-up for KL race
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Hyrox Malaysia has apologised and said it will not extend its partnership with beer brand Carlsberg for its upcoming Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 fitness race.
The Youth and Sports Ministry had earlier today refused to approve the fitness event unless the organisers cut ties with the alcohol sponsor.
In a statement posted on its Instagram account today, the organiser said the regional announcement naming Carlsberg as a partner had caused concern and offence.
“We understand why this has caused concern and offence, and we should have given greater consideration to the religious beliefs and cultural values of our Malaysian community.
“We got this wrong, and we take responsibility for that,” it said.
The organiser said the decision to keep the partnership out of the Malaysia race was made together with Carlsberg.
It also addressed participants directly, saying it recognised the time and effort they had put into training, and added that it looked forward to seeing them at the start line.
Hyrox Kuala Lumpur 2026 is scheduled to run from December 10 to 13 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec).
The statement came after the Youth and Sports Ministry said earlier today that it would withhold approval for the event until the alcohol sponsorship was terminated. It also required all related branding, logos and promotional material to be removed from marketing channels and the competition venue.
The ministry said the organiser’s licence application was still under review, and that the government had neither approved the event nor provided any funding for it.
It cited Article 5.2 of the Safe Sport Code (3rd Edition, 2024). The article bars companies involved in tobacco, e-cigarettes and alcoholic beverages from sponsoring, advertising, merchandising, offering prizes or displaying trademarks at sports activities sanctioned or supported by the ministry and its agencies.
“The ministry will not compromise in ensuring a safe and healthy sports environment for all participants,” Youth and Sports Minister Mohammed Taufiq Johari said in a statement.
The ministry also reminded the organisers that running a sports event without a licence from the Commissioner of Sports Malaysia breaches Section 36(1) of the Sports Development Act 1997. Offenders face a fine of between RM50,000 and RM500,000, up to five years’ imprisonment, or both.

Title: ‘Do not abuse your popularity’: Judge delivers warning after preacher Da’i Syed beats rape charge in split decision
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — A Court of Appeal judge has advised celebrity preacher Da’I Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, not to abuse his popularity or take advantage of vulnerable individuals.
Judge Datuk Azman Abdullah, who chaired a three-member panel, said exploiting individuals who were emotionally vulnerable could tarnish the reputation of those who projected a religious image.
“I would like to offer some advice to the appellant. This advice is not directed solely at you. We often come across cases involving rape, sodomy and similar offences occurring at pondok (religious) schools, allegedly committed by teachers...this reflects poorly on society,” he said.
Syed Shah Iqmal, 31, who was standing in the dock, was seen nodding as he listened to the judge’s remarks.
Earlier, in a 2-1 majority decision, Judges Datuk Azman Abdullah and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid acquitted and discharged Syed Shah Iqmal of a charge of raping a woman in 2019, while the third panel member, Judge Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, dissented and would have upheld the conviction and sentence meted out by the lower court.
The panel made the decision after allowing Syed Shah Iqmal’s final appeal against his conviction and sentence of 10 years’ imprisonment and three strokes of the cane, imposed by the Shah Alam Sessions Court.
After Judge Azman delivered the majority decision, Syed Shah Iqmal was seen weeping in the dock, while his wife, Hana Ismail, who was seated in the public gallery, was also seen crying.
On Dec 10, 2020, Syed Shah Iqmal pleaded not guilty to raping a 23-year-old woman at a condominium unit in I-City, Section 7, here, at about 1.35 am on Sept 11, 2019.
The charge was framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
On April 10, 2023, the Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted and discharged him of the charge after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case at the close of its case.
However, the Shah Alam High Court subsequently allowed the prosecution’s appeal and ordered Syed Shah Iqmal to enter his defence. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya rejects foreign pressure to hike defence spending, maintains non-aligned stance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 5 — Malaysia is not obligated to heed the recommendation made by major powers to raise its defence spending to 5 per cent of Gross National Product (GNP), Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin told the Dewan Rakyat today.
Khaled suggested the push for more defence spending only serves the interest of foreign powers who want neutral nations on the frontlines during major conflicts, in allusion seemingly made towards countries that are seen as hostile to China.
“There are countries recommending that we raise our defence expenditure to five per cent of GNP. The intention is that these major powers want us out in front whenever there is a clash, conflict, or war,” Khaled said in reply to William Leong (PH-Selayang).
Malaysia and Southeast Asia have long committed to a non-aligned foreign policy that had been formally codified amid geopolitical tension caused by the Cold War.
Khaled said Mindef will manage its defence budget based on its own national capabilities.
Putrajaya allocates roughly 1.0 to 1.1 per cent of national output to defence spending annually, according to Malaysian Defence, an online defence magazine. Under Budget 2026 the Ministry of Defence was allocated RM21.7 billion.
“We want to state clearly that we are not married to any major power. We are free, we are neutral, and we spend and allocate funds according to our own capability,” the minister said, adding that the country’s military doctrine is purely defensive.
“Our defence doctrine is meant to defend the nation, not to attack any country,” he said.

Title: Former Sungai Ujong Undang and five others fail to halt contempt proceedings
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 4 — Former Undang Luak of Sungai Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak and five others today failed in a bid to halt committal proceedings against them after the Court of Appeal dismissed their application for a stay pending the disposal of their appeal.
A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously dismissed the application and ordered the six appellants to pay RM60,000 in costs to the respondents, namely Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU) and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin.
The six applicants, comprising four Undangs and two chieftains, had appealed against the Seremban High Court’s decision granting the DKU and Raja Norazli leave to initiate committal proceedings against them for allegedly breaching an injunction order.
The six appellants, besides Mubarak, are Undang Luak of Jelebu Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Undang Luak of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Undang Luak of Rembau Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri, and Shahbandar of Sungai Ujong Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid.
Justice Amarjeet said that the committal proceedings directly involved the court’s jurisdiction to prevent undue interference with the administration of justice and to preserve the authority of the court in the public interest.
“In view of their nature, committal applications ought to be dealt with expeditiously in the interest of justice,” said Justice Amarjeet when delivering the bench’s decision.
He further said that the issue raised by the six concerning their purported immunity should be determined after, and not before, the substantive hearing of the committal proceedings.
“The very issue ought to be fully ventilated and determined at the committal proceedings during the substantive stage,” said the judge.
Justice Amarjeet also pointed out that the court found that the appellants had not approached the matter with clean hands, as they were seeking equitable relief while simultaneously pursuing a separate judicial review application at the Kuala Lumpur High Court concerning the same issues.
He said, more importantly, the appellants had failed to disclose to the High Court the existence of the injunction order and the fact that leave to commence committal proceedings had already been granted against them.
The legal dispute originated on May 5 this year when Mubarak and five others filed an originating summons at the High Court to obtain a copy of the minutes of a special DKU meeting held on April 17. Among the contents of the meeting minutes was a decision to remove Mubarak as Undang Luak of Sungai Ujong.
On June 5 this year, the High Court granted an ad interim injunction to preserve the status quo, maintaining the existing composition of the DKU and Raja Norazli’s position as its secretary, pending the determination of issues relating to jurisdiction and justiciability, or until further order of the court.
However, Raja Norazli claimed that media reports on the same day showed that the plaintiffs, particularly Maarof, had been involved in the purported appointment of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan under Article 11 of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959, despite the injunction order still being in force.
He alleged that the appointment was made in defiance of the court order, prompting the DKU and Raja Norazli to seek leave from the High Court to commence committal proceedings against the six individuals for contempt of court. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s first female education D-G Asiah Abu Samah dies at 89
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 4 — Renowned education figure Tan Sri Dr Asiah Abu Samah died at a private hospital in the capital today. She was 89.
Asiah, the first woman to serve as Malaysia’s director-general of education, died at 5 am.
According to a circulated notice, funeral prayers will be held after Zohor prayers at Masjid At-Taqwa in Taman Tun Dr Ismail, followed by burial at the Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery here.
Born on March 1, 1937, in Parit, Perak, Asiah made significant contributions to the development and advancement of Malaysia’s education system.
She studied at Universiti Malaya in Singapore, where she obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in History and a Diploma in Education before beginning her teaching career at Penang Free School in 1961.
She later served as a language lecturer at an institute in Lembah Pantai before being appointed principal of Tunku Kurshiah College (TKC) in Seremban, a position she held from Dec 1966 to Sept 1970.
Meanwhile, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek described Asiah’s passing as a major loss to the nation’s education sector, particularly given her contributions to the development of the national education system.
“I am deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Tan Sri Asiah Abu Samah, former director-general of education.
“As the first woman to hold this position, she paved the way for women to take on leadership roles in the country’s education sector. Her contributions will always be remembered by those of us who continue the responsibility of educating Malaysia’s children,” she said in a Facebook post.
Fadhlina also extended her condolences to Asiah’s family on behalf of the Education Ministry.
“May her family be granted strength and patience as they cope with the loss of their loved one. May Allah SWT forgive her sins, bless her soul and grant her a place among the faithful.
“Thank you, Tan Sri, for your dedication and invaluable service to the nation’s education sector,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Penang Hospital to complete new blocks in 2027 and 2029 to tackle overcrowding
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 4 — Two new blocks at Penang Hospital are expected to help ease congestion at its Emergency and Trauma Department, with the women’s and children’s block scheduled for completion in 2027 and the specialist clinics and wards block in 2029.
State Youth, Sports and Health Committee chairman Daniel Gooi Zi Sen said the projects formed part of the hospital’s long-term plan to address overcrowding caused by a shortage of ward beds.
He said the Health Ministry was also implementing measures under its patient flow management guidelines, including diverting non-emergency patients from the department through stronger primary healthcare services and better screening at entry points.
“These measures include extending the operating hours of health clinics to allow high-risk patients to be admitted directly to hospital wards, as well as working with nearby private clinics under the MADANI Medical Scheme and PeKa B40 for low-risk cases.”
Gooi was replying to Gooi Hsiao Leung (PH-Bukit Tengah), who asked about measures to address congestion and long waiting times at the department during the State Assembly sitting today.
Gooi noted that the ministry had also strengthened the Bed Management Unit, introduced the Open Bed Policy and expanded the use of multidisciplinary wards to ensure patients could be placed in any available bed.
He said discharge and post-treatment processes had also been streamlined through a Discharge Lounge, with a target of freeing up beds before noon to accommodate new patients.
Statistically, Gooi said the proportion of critical patients in the Red Zone rose to 7.14 per cent by July 2026, up from 6.79 per cent in 2025, while semi-critical Yellow Zone cases rose to 19.81 per cent from 18.92 per cent.
Green Zone cases remained almost unchanged at 40.06 per cent, compared with 40.13 per cent in 2025, while non-emergency cases (LOCUM) declined to 32.99 per cent from 34.16 per cent, he added. — Bernama

Title: Bridge collapses in Selangor as flash floods hit Sungai Buloh and Petaling
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH, Nov 4 — Several major roads and areas in Selangor were affected by flash floods following continuous heavy rain since early today, with a bridge along Jalan Kubu Gajah spanning Sungai Subang in the Petaling district collapsing.
According to the Petaling District Public Works Department (JKR), the bridge collapsed at about 2 am after strong currents in Sungai Subang eroded the riverbanks, following rainfall of 48 millimetres recorded at the Paya Jaras Hilir station.
The collapse completely cut off the main route linking Kampung Kubu Gajah and Paya Jaras Hilir, prompting authorities to close the road to all vehicles for safety reasons.
To ease traffic disruption, a Traffic Management Plan (TMP) has been activated, with motorists heading to Merbau Sempak and Kubu Gajah diverted via Jalan Merbau Sempak towards Masjid Nurul Iman.
Motorists travelling to Paya Jaras Hilir can use Jalan Paya Jaras Hilir via Federal Route 54 (FT54).
JKR said a temporary Bailey bridge would be installed as a medium-term measure to restore access between the affected areas.
Meanwhile, Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said flash floods also affected Sungai Buloh, Paya Jaras, Kampung Melayu Subang, Rawang and several areas in Shah Alam.
In a related development, floodwaters on major highways have begun to recede, including at the Shah Alam interchange, based on closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage monitored by the Malaysian Highway Authority’s (LLM) Traffic Management Centre.
An LLM spokesman said the right and middle lanes at the Shah Alam interchange heading north had been reopened to traffic.
“However, the southbound lanes at the interchange remain temporarily closed to allow debris to be cleared and safety inspections to be carried out before they are fully reopened.
“So far, no other highways have been reported to be affected by flooding,” he told Bernama. — Bernama
